A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ringleader ASGD work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison. The former Appendices B–E in v1 correspond to C–F in v3.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figure 1 report original training simulations on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, comparing convergence under heterogeneous client data and computation delays.

after.justification: Section 6 and Figure 1 retain the original MNIST and Fashion-MNIST simulation results, including convergence curves and uncertainty bands.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same gradient table, buffering, gradient collection, and sequential worker updates. The adaptation for varying computation times is retained from v1 Appendix B in v3 Appendix C. The corrected appendix formula does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST with heterogeneous client data and simulated computation delays. No dataset, task, or evaluated scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 1 compares Ringleader ASGD with Malenia SGD and IA2SGD in both versions. Table 1 retains its method membership; its added lower-bound row is a theoretical reference, not a newly evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 6 retains 100 clients, Dirichlet concentration 0.1, the same two-layer MLP, minibatch size 4, delay construction, stepsize sweep, and full-dataset gradient-norm-versus-runtime metric. The new model discussion does not revise experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports additional empirical ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness tests, or error analyses. The adversarial timing example is retained in v1 Appendix B.2 and v3 Appendix C.2; the new communication discussion is conceptual.

E5.justification: Both versions report 30 seeds per method, median convergence curves, and interquartile-range bands. No run count or statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Figure 1 and its caption are visually identical, including convergence curves and uncertainty bands. Both retain the finding that Ringleader ASGD converges faster than Malenia SGD and IA2SGD. Table 1's added lower-bound row displays a theoretical comparison already described in v1.

T1.justification: The Lemma 6 proof in v3 Appendix D.2 restores the within-worker minibatch averages missing from the displayed estimator identity in v1 Appendix C.2. This corrects a local mathematical inconsistency; the assumptions, theorem bounds, and remaining derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The principal optimality, resource-utilization, parameter-free design, and varying-computation-time contributions remain the same. v3 foregrounds the condition L = O(L_f) in Section 1.1 and Remark 5.1, but v1 already explicitly applies that qualification through Table 1 and footnote 1.

C2.justification: New Appendix B expands the interpretation of the computation-only model. Beyond v1's instantaneous-communication assumption, it explains that avoiding waiting does not itself reduce communication cost and that explicit communication costs require additional mechanisms and a different theoretical framework.

D1.justification: Section 6 retains the same preprocessing, partitioning procedure, architecture, minibatch size, delay generation, stepsize grid, and curve-smoothing details. No implementation resources or code/data access instructions are added or removed.

R1.justification: New Appendix B elaborates the relationship to communication-efficient methods, describing compression and local updates, including FedAvg and Tyurin et al. (2024b), as complementary to asynchrony. The bibliography and existing related-work section remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 inserts an explanatory Appendix B, renumbers the former Appendices B–E as C–F, adds Remark 5.1, and makes localized wording and typographical corrections. Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains an explicit lower-bound row and changes check/cross styling. Figure 1 remains unchanged. Other presentation differences mainly involve spacing and page reflow, including the acknowledgment placement.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision by explaining the communication-model boundary in Appendix B, making the existing smoothness qualification more prominent, and displaying the lower bound directly in Table 1. It also fixes the missing minibatch averages in the variance-proof identity. These are useful, limited improvements; the algorithm, theorem bounds, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
